source: Classic test design techniques (common testing knowledge: ISTQB, Kaner, Myers). Descriptions are ours.

heuristics.name: Equivalence classes
heuristics.description: Inputs that should be handled the same way form a class; one value per class is enough to start.
heuristics.apply: Split each input into valid and invalid groups, and test one typical value from each group.

heuristics.name: Pairwise combinations
heuristics.description: Most bugs from combining settings need only two of them to interact, so covering every pair is efficient.
heuristics.apply: List options that can be combined, then pick tests so each pair of values appears together at least once.

heuristics.name: Decision table
heuristics.description: Rules with several conditions are easy to get wrong for some combination of those conditions.
heuristics.apply: Write each business rule as conditions and outcomes, and test every combination of the conditions.

heuristics.name: Error guessing
heuristics.description: Experience says where developers often slip: off-by-one, empty cases, time zones, rounding.
heuristics.apply: List the mistakes you'd expect in this kind of feature and write one test for each.

heuristics.name: Error messages
heuristics.description: An error message should say what went wrong and what to do, without technical noise or leaked internals.
heuristics.apply: Cause each error you can and read the message: is it clear, correct, and free of stack traces or internal details?

heuristics.name: Round trip
heuristics.description: Data that goes out and comes back (save and load, export and import) should come back the same.
heuristics.apply: Save or export something, load or import it again, and compare with the original field by field.

heuristics.name: Touring
heuristics.description: Following a theme through the product (money, landmarks, the longest path) finds areas nobody planned tests for.
heuristics.apply: Pick a theme, like everything to do with money or every screen reachable from the menu, and visit all of it.

heuristics.name: Permissions matrix
heuristics.description: Each kind of user should see and do only what their role allows.
heuristics.apply: List roles and actions, then try each action as each role, including as a visitor who isn't logged in.

heuristics.name: Oracle by comparison
heuristics.description: Two ways of getting the same answer (the page and the API, two screens) should agree.
heuristics.apply: Get the same number or list two ways and compare them.
